subject: Amazon Marketplace — solution summary + SKU visibility question
thread_body:
From: Sophia Holt <sophia.holt@acme-analytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inquiry: Listing SKU visibility and customer-facing summary

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme is excited about the Dedicated offering. Before we start the seller registration, I wanted to confirm two things that matter for our procurement and GTM folks:

1) Visibility: if we list multiple SKUs (dev/test/prod tiers) in the Amazon offer, can we control which SKUs are visible in the marketplace to end customers? Our legal team wants dev/test hidden from search.
2) Copy: we need a one-paragraph product description and a short solution summary for the listing page. Can you share a version we can include in our marketplace asset bundle?

Attaching a draft of what procurement asked for (see sku_visibility_matrix.csv).

Appreciate any quick guidance.

—Sophia
Procurement Lead, Acme Analytics

---

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Holt <sophia.holt@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Listing SKU visibility and customer-facing summary

Hi Sophia — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes, visibility can be scoped per-SKU, and attached is a concise product summary plus a one-pager we typically share with ISVs.

Notes on visibility:
- Marketplace offers support SKU-level visibility and entitlements. We can set the dev/test SKUs to be private (not searchable) and only the prod SKU public.
- For deeper control we recommend using a staged AMI/tagging pattern and enforcing entitlement checks on the first-run flow so that even if someone accesses a dev SKU, they cannot provision without the right entitlements.

Im attaching a suggested marketplace description and a solution one-pager (solution_one_pager.pdf) and the SKU mapping we discussed. Ben / Karthik — can you review the short copy and confirm there are no compliance red flags? Vanessa — can you also confirm that the hero image meets AWS Marketplace guidelines (size / claims)?

Next steps: if this looks good to you, well package the assets and Ill introduce you to our AWS listing coordinator to schedule the submission window.

Thanks,
Steph
Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: solution_one_pager.pdf, sku_visibility_matrix.csv

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Listing SKU visibility and customer-facing summary

Steph — quick pass below. I kept bullets we can drop into the product detail area. No legal issues from my side but two small asks:

- Remove the phrase "enterprise-grade immutable logs" from the public copy unless we can validate with the audits team (sounds stronger than our standard wording).
- For the pricing callout, recommend using "starting at" language instead of an explicit $/hour unless Acme wants to display exact pricing (AWS has specific pricing UI rules).

Suggested product blurb (one line):
Redwood Inference: fast, predictable LLM inference with flexible deployment — hosted, dedicated, and private options for production workloads.

Longer solution summary (3 lines):
Deliver consistent low-latency inference for customer-facing applications with optimized GPU serving, intelligent caching, and orchestration across hosted and private deployments. Offer configurable SLAs and dedicated capacity to support regulated workloads.

Ill leave final claims validation to Karthik.

—Ben
Head of Marketplace Strategy

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T12:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Listing SKU visibility and customer-facing summary

Ben — thanks, that language looks fine with two small edits:
1) Change "configurable SLAs" to "SLA-backed options" to avoid implying the SLA itself is configurable by any buyer.
2) Swap "intelligent caching" for "workload-aware caching" which matches our product docs.

Final recommended summary (I suggest we send this to Acme):
Redwood Inference — fast, predictable LLM inference with flexible deployment modes: hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC) deployments. Deliver consistent low-latency inference through optimized GPU serving, workload-aware caching, and orchestration across environments. SLA-backed options and enterprise security integrations for regulated workloads.

Vanessa — hero asset: the png attached (product-hero-asset-v2.png) contains a claims ladder. Can you confirm its compliant (no pricing or unverifiable performance claims)? If not, Ill remove the callouts.

—Karthik
Applied ML / Inference Optimization

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Listing SKU visibility and customer-facing summary

All, I reviewed product-hero-asset-v2.png and the one-pager. Minor tweaks:
- Trim the graphic claim that lists specific latency numbers (we can add a footnote to a benchmark page instead).
- Replace a screenshot showing private deployment with our generic diagram (per AWS image policy on customer screenshots).

Ill prepare an AWS-compliant image and update the one-pager to remove the explicit latency callouts. Will upload both to the Drive link in an hour.

—Vanessa
Product Marketing

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Holt <sophia.holt@acme-analytics.com>, marketplace-seller-support@amazon.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Listing SKU visibility and customer-facing summary

Hi Sophia — quick update and next steps: weve incorporated internal feedback and have a final draft ready. Answers:

- SKU visibility: confirmable. We will mark dev/test SKUs as non-public and only make prod SKU searchable. We will also include an entitlement check for dev/test to prevent accidental provisioning.
- Listing copy: see the suggested product blurb and 3-line solution summary below; Vanessa will upload an AWS-compliant hero image and an updated one-pager to the shared Drive by end of day.

Suggested product blurb (for marketplace short summary):
Redwood Inference — fast, predictable LLM inference across hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Suggested solution summary (for product detail):
Deliver consistent low-latency inference through optimized GPU serving, workload-aware caching, and orchestration across environments. SLA-backed options and enterprise security integrations support regulated workloads and production-grade applications.

Attachments: solution_one_pager.pdf (updated soon), sku_visibility_matrix.csv, product-hero-asset-v2.png (to be replaced in Drive)

If that aligns with Acmes procurement, Ill introduce you to our AWS listing coordinator to schedule the submission window and confirm the SKU visibility settings in the seller portal.

Would you like me to make the marketplace submission on Acmes behalf (we can do a co-sell-managed submission), or would you prefer we hand you the asset package and you submit?

Looking forward to next steps.

—Steph
Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
